gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's '12kW bypass powers HVACs' claim for the Apex 300 home kit only holds while grid power is feeding the unit; in an outage a single Apex 300 can supply only its inverter's 3,840 W, which is 16 A at 240 V, so a Texas central AC on the kit's sub panel would run on the battery alone during a blackout at well under a third of that bypass figure.
standout_why: I compared homebattery.guide (cited) and theenergycollective.com (cited). Neither mentions the BLUETTI Apex or Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus, transfer-switch or inlet kits, neutral bonding, or the difference between grid-bypass watts and battery watts. theenergycollective does cover part of the AC problem: it says a 2-ton AC needs about 5,800 W to start and that EcoFlow's 4,000 W kit 'can't run a central AC alongside much else'. So the general warning that a power station is too small for central AC is already out there. What no rival says is that the maker's own '12kW … HVACs' figure depends on the grid being up, or that the kit is sold in Single and Parallel versions that you must match to how many units you own. I scored it 2 rather than 3 because the AC-sizing idea is partly covered.
kit_items: power station: BLUETTI Apex 300 (3,840 W continuous, 120/240 V from one unit). StorageReview says a single unit produces 240 V because it has two inverters, so you do not need a second unit to get 240 V.
expansion battery: BLUETTI B300K, which brings the system to 5,529.6 Wh. A single Apex 300 delivered 2.39 kWh in StorageReview's test, which is not enough for a Texas outage of a day or more.

home tie-in: BLUETTI Apex 300 Home Integration Kit, 'Single Apex 300' variant. This is the sub panel with a 50 A inlet and the cable that connects the station to the house. Buy the Parallel variant only if you own two Apex 300s.
optional DC/USB: BLUETTI Hub D1 ($299). StorageReview says the Apex 300 has no USB-C, USB-A, car-socket or Anderson outputs without it.

findings.product: BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K + Home Backup Kit (Single Apex 300)
findings.label: HVAC claim on the maker's page
findings.value: '12kW bypass powers HVACs, EVs, and more'; product card says 3,840W
findings.source_title: Apex 300 + B300K + Home Backup Kit (Single Apex 300) – BLUETTI
findings.note: Bypass means grid power passing straight through the unit, so it disappears in an outage. With the grid down the limit is the inverter: 3,840 W / 240 V = 16 A at 240 V. The page does not mention soft starters or neutral bonding.

findings.label: Inverter output, and where the 12 kW figure comes from
findings.value: 3,840 W max total, 120V/240V; 14-50R rated 120/240V 50A; BLUETTI's 'up to 12kW' bypass via the 50A port was not tested
findings.source_title: StorageReview, Kevin OBrien: BLUETTI Apex 300 review (dated 2026-11-09)
findings.note: StorageReview says the 12 kW bypass is BLUETTI's own claim for EV charging and HVAC, and it has no measured data for central AC or well pumps.

findings.label: Standard AC charging inlet
findings.value: 120 V, 15 A, with a 1,800 W limit in bypass; 50 A in/out only through the P050A port and BLUETTI's 14-50P cable
findings.source_title: StorageReview, Kevin OBrien: BLUETTI Apex 300 review
findings.note: Fast recharging from a 240 V generator needs a 50 A cord into the P050A port. The standard inlet caps charging at 1,800 W.

findings.label: Usable energy measured by StorageReview
findings.value: 2.39 kWh of 2,764.8 Wh (86%) on its own; 7.38 kWh with two B300K
findings.source_title: StorageReview, Kevin OBrien: BLUETTI Apex 300 review
findings.note: Recharging took 3.30 kWh for the single unit and 10.01 kWh with two packs. At a 3 kW AC load, 2.39 kWh lasts about 48 minutes (my arithmetic).

findings.label: Adapter that is easy to miss
findings.value: Hub D1 ($299) required for USB-C, USB-A, cigarette-lighter, DC5521 and Anderson outputs
findings.source_title: StorageReview, Kevin OBrien: BLUETTI Apex 300 review
findings.note: BLUETTI's store lists the Hub D1 Power Hub for Apex 300 at $299.00 (storecheck, 2026-11-14).

findings.label: Variant trap
findings.note: Read through storecheck. The kit is listed as compatible with the Apex 300 only. Match the variant to how many Apex 300s you own.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus + Home Backup Kit
findings.label: 240 V output blocked while charging from 120 V
findings.value: 'The 240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC.'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Home Backup Kit – Anker SOLIX
findings.note: Most portable inverter generators charge over 120 V. Using one in an outage switches off the 240 V circuits (central AC, well pump) on the transfer switch. The same page says the generator adapter only supports a single F3800 Plus unit, and the F3800 Plus + Home Backup Kit showed as Sold Out.

findings.label: 240 V port rating
findings.value: NEMA L14-30R: 120V/240V, 25 A max, 6,000 W max
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Home Backup Kit – Anker SOLIX
findings.note: The page says it 'powers fridges to central AC' but does not mention soft starters.
